premises: Cryo-rolling increases hardness difference between B2 and L12 phases compared to cold-rolling
Increased hardness difference leads to strain partitioning, with B2 accumulating lower strain during cryo-rolling
Lower strain in B2 during cryo-rolling results in incomplete recrystallization, forming coarse recovered B2 regions upon annealing
The resulting heterogeneous hierarchical microstructure (fine lamellar, ultrafine FCC, coarse FCC, coarse recovered B2) enhances strength and ductility
Back stress strengthening from strain gradients at domain interfaces is the mechanism for simultaneous improvement
